have authority to agree a Margin Threshold in excess of $500,000 for either the Buyer or the Seller.
096: •  Any proposal to raise the Buyer (Voss Bank) threshold above $250,000 is presumptively unacceptable absent exceptional credit quality of the counterparty (e.g., a sovereign wealth fund or central bank with a AAA credit rating). Raising the Buyer threshold above $250,000 reduces Voss Bank's ability to call for margin promptly and increases the risk that a material margin deficit will accumulate before a call can be made.
097: •  Any proposal to eliminate the Margin Threshold entirely (i.e., to set the threshold at zero) should be viewed with caution, even though it is ostensibly more protective of Voss Bank's interests. A zero threshold creates significant operational burden and may result in a high volume of de minimis margin calls that strain settlement capacity. If a counterparty proposes a zero threshold, the desk should propose $250,000 symmetric as a more practical alternative.
098: 4.4 — Margin Call Mechanics
099: In addition to the Margin Threshold, the following margin call mechanics are standard Annex I elections and should be included in all GMRA negotiations:
100: •  Margin call cut-off time: 10:00 a.m. London time. This is the time by which a margin call must be received by the recipient party in order to trigger a same-day settlement obligation.
101: •  Calls received before cut-off: same-day settlement. If a valid margin call is received before 10:00 a.m. London time on a business day, the responding party must deliver the required Margin Securities or Cash Margin on the same business day.
102: •  Calls received at or after cut-off: next business day settlement. If a valid margin call is received at or after 10:00 a.m. London time, the responding party's obligation to deliver Margin Securities or Cash Margin is deferred to the next business day.
103: The 10:00 a.m. London time cut-off is non-negotiable. It aligns with the London Branch's operational cycle and with the settlement windows of the Branch's primary settlement systems (Clearstream and DTC). Counterparty proposals to move the cut-off to a later time (e.g., 12:00 noon London time or 10:00 a.m. New York time) should be resisted. If the counterparty insists on a later cut-off, consult Operations (London) to confirm whether a later cut-off can be operationally accommodated before making any concession.
104: Section 5 — Net Exposure Cap
105: 5.1 — Standard Cap
106: The Net Exposure Cap is the maximum aggregate net credit exposure that Voss Bank is prepared to accept to a single counterparty under the GMRA. It is set on a counterparty-by-counterparty basis by the Credit Committee in Zürich, based on the counterparty's credit profile, the nature and expected volume of the trading relationship, and Voss Bank's overall portfolio concentration limits.
107: For the Meridian Capital Securities LLC relationship, the approved Net Exposure Cap is $1,500,000,000 (one billion five hundred million US dollars). This cap was approved by the Credit Committee on 7 March 2025 as part of the pre-negotiation credit approval for the Meridian GMRA.
108: The Net Exposure Cap is expressed as a single aggregate figure and is not broken down by Transaction type, collateral type, or tenor. It applies to the aggregate net mark-to-market exposure across all outstanding Transactions under the GMRA at any point in time, after giving effect to haircuts and any margin transfers.
109: 5.2 — Negotiation Guidance
110: The Net Exposure Cap is not typically a negotiated term in the traditional sense. It is a unilateral credit limit set by Voss Bank to reflect its own credit risk appetite, and it is inserted into Annex I as a Buyer election. The counterparty is free to set its own exposure cap (if any) on its side, and Voss Bank will not object to a counterparty's unilateral cap unless it is so low as to render the trading relationship commercially unviable.
111: The desk should be aware of, and resist, the following counterparty proposals relating to the Net Exposure Cap:
112: •  Bilateral cap. Some counterparties will propose that the Net Exposure Cap be bilateral — i.e., that it apply equally to both parties, so that neither party's aggregate net exposure may exceed the stated cap. This is inappropriate because the cap reflects Voss Bank's credit assessment of the counterparty, not a mutual assessment. A bilateral cap would constrain Voss Bank's ability to manage its own exposure unilaterally. The desk should reject bilateral cap proposals.
113: •  Indexation. Some counterparties (particularly US broker-dealers) will propose that the Net Exposure Cap be indexed to the counterparty's own net capital or regulatory capital ratios — for example, that the cap be set at a fixed percentage of the counterparty's excess net capital under SEC Rule 15c3-1. Indexation introduces variability and unpredictability into the cap and creates a risk that the cap will decrease at precisely the time when the counterparty's credit quality is deteriorating (and when Voss Bank most needs the protection of a firm cap). The desk should reject indexation proposals.
114: •  Periodic review. The Credit Committee reviews Net Exposure Caps as part of its regular credit review cycle (typically annually, or more frequently if triggered by a credit event). The desk may agree to include language in Annex I stating that the cap is "subject to periodic review," provided that such language does not create any obligation on Voss Bank to increase the cap or any right of the counterparty to request an increase.
115: Section 6 — Substitution of Collateral
116: 6.1 — Preferred Position
117: Voss Bank's preferred position on substitution of Purchased Securities is that the Seller's right to substitute collateral requires prior written consent of the Buyer (Voss Bank). Consent may be given or withheld in Buyer's sole and absolute discretion, and no obligation to act reasonably or in good faith shall apply to Buyer's exercise of the consent right.
118: This position ensures that Voss Bank can assess the HQLA eligibility, haircut adequacy, and concentration limits of any proposed substitute collateral before the substitution takes effect. It also preserves Voss Bank's ability to refuse substitution at times of market stress, when the quality and liquidity of substitute collateral may be difficult to assess in real time.
119: The desk should propose the prior-consent position in all Turn 1 drafts. Counterparties with active collateral management programmes will frequently resist this position, arguing that the consent requirement impedes their ability to optimise their collateral pools. The desk should be prepared for pushback and should use the prior-consent position as a negotiating lever — conceding it in exchange for concessions on other terms, such as haircuts or margin thresholds.
120: 6.2 — Acceptable Fallback
121: Voss Bank may accept a no-consent substitution framework — that is, a framework under which the Seller may substitute Purchased Securities without obtaining Buyer's prior consent — where all of the following conditions are satisfied simultaneously:
122: (a) The Seller provides at least 1 business day's prior notice to the Buyer of the proposed substitution, specifying the Purchased Securities to be withdrawn and the proposed substitute collateral in reasonable detail (including ISIN, nominal amount, Market Value, and credit rating).
123: (b) The substitute collateral must be of the same or better Eligible Collateral category as the Purchased Securities being replaced. For these purposes, sovereign collateral may only be replaced with sovereign collateral of the same or better credit quality; corporate collateral may be replaced with sovereign collateral or with corporate collateral of the same or better credit rating and with the same or shorter residual maturity. A "downgrade" in collateral category — for example, substituting corporate bonds for sovereign bonds, or lower-rated corporate bonds for higher-rated corporate bonds — is not permitted under this framework.
124: (c) At the time of the proposed substitution, there is no outstanding Margin Deficit in respect of any Transaction under the GMRA. If a Margin Deficit exists at the time of the proposed substitution, the Seller must first cure the Margin Deficit (by delivering additional Margin Securities or Cash Margin) before effecting the substitution.
125: If all three conditions are satisfied, no Buyer consent is required. The substitution may proceed upon expiry of the notice period, provided that the conditions remain satisfied at the time the substitution is effected.
126: This fallback was used to resolve the substitution issue in the Meridian negotiation at Turn 3. Meridian initially proposed a no-consent substitution right with no notice period and no quality constraints. Voss Bank countered with the prior-consent position. The fallback described above — 1 business day notice, same-or-better quality, no Margin Deficit — was proposed by Alistair Fenn of Calder Stone Partners LLP as a compromise, and was accepted by Meridian's counsel (Rachel S. Okonkwo of PAG) by email on 14 April 2025. This fallback is approved for general use in future negotiations.
127: 6.3 — Walk-Away
128: The following substitution rights are unacceptable and constitute a walk-away:
129: •  Any substitution right that permits a downgrade in collateral quality — for example, substituting BBB-rated corporate bonds for A-rated corporate bonds, or substituting corporate bonds for sovereign bonds.
130: •  Any substitution right that permits substitution during a Margin Deficit — this would allow the Seller to withdraw collateral at precisely the time when Voss Bank's exposure is already inadequately covered.
131: •  Any substitution right that does not require at least 1 business day's prior notice — this would prevent Voss Bank from conducting even a basic assessment of the proposed substitute collateral before the substitution takes effect.
132: •  Any substitution right that permits substitution of collateral with a residual maturity exceeding 10 years (for corporate bonds) or with a credit rating below the minimum ratings thresholds specified in Sections 3.1 and 3.2.
133: Section 7 — Repricing / Mini Close-Out
134: 7.1 — Preferred Position
135: Voss Bank elects a repricing / mini close-out option (commonly referred to as a "repricing" or "re-rate" provision) exercisable at the 90th calendar day of any outstanding Transaction, or at each quarterly anniversary of the Purchase Date, whichever is later. The repricing right allows Voss Bank (as Buyer) to terminate and reprice the Transaction at the then-current Market Value of the Purchased Securities, adjusted for the applicable haircut, with the effect that the Purchase Price and Repurchase Price are reset to reflect current market conditions.
136: Exercise of the repricing right requires 2 business days' prior written notice to the Seller. Notice may be given by email to the Seller's designated notice address (as specified in Annex I) or by such other means as the parties may agree.
137: 7.2 — Rationale
138: Repricing rights protect Voss Bank against cumulative drift in collateral value on term trades. In a term repo transaction, the Purchase Price is fixed at inception based on the Market Value of the Purchased Securities at that time, adjusted for the applicable haircut. Over the life of the trade, the Market Value of the Purchased Securities may change — due to interest rate movements, credit spread widening or tightening, or other market factors — while the Purchase Price remains fixed.
139: The margin maintenance provisions of the GMRA (Paragraph 4) provide some protection against collateral value decline by requiring the Seller to deliver additional margin when the Margin Deficit exceeds the Margin Threshold. However, margin calls alone may not fully cure mark-to-market exposure on long-dated term trades, particularly where:
140: (a) the Margin Threshold is set at a level that allows a material margin deficit to accumulate before a call is triggered;
141: (b) the frequency of mark-to-market valuation is limited (e.g., daily valuation may miss intra-day volatility spikes);
142: (c) the collateral has declined in credit quality or liquidity to the point where its Market Value, even after margin top-ups, no longer provides adequate protection; or
143: (d) the Seller is unable or unwilling to deliver margin in response to a call, creating a period of unhedged exposure before an Event of Default is triggered.
144: The repricing right addresses these risks by allowing Voss Bank to periodically "reset" the economics of the trade to current market conditions. In effect, the repricing operates as a mini close-out: the original Transaction is terminated, the net settlement amount is calculated, and a new Transaction is simultaneously entered into at current prices. This mechanism is particularly important for term trades with a duration exceeding 60 days, where the cumulative risk of collateral value drift is most acute.
145: 7.3 — Acceptable Fallback
146: The preferred position — repricing at the 90th calendar day or quarterly, whichever is later, with 2 business days' prior notice — is also the fallback minimum. Voss Bank does not have a broader fallback range for the repricing provision; the preferred position represents the minimum acceptable level of protection.
147: Voss Bank may accept a counterparty proposal that aligns with this formulation even if the counterparty characterises it as a compromise or a concession. For example, if the counterparty proposes "repricing at quarterly intervals with 2 business days' notice," this is substantively equivalent to the Voss Bank position (since quarterly repricing is consistent with the "90th calendar day or quarterly, whichever is later" formulation) and should be accepted.
148: The desk should note that the repricing right is exercisable at Voss Bank's option — it is not an automatic repricing. Voss Bank is not obligated to exercise the repricing right at any particular interval. The right provides flexibility to reprice when market conditions warrant, without creating an obligation to reprice when conditions are stable.
149: 7.4 — Walk-Away
150: No repricing right at all is unacceptable for term trades with a duration exceeding 60 days. This is a firm walk-away, and it applies regardless of the counterparty's credit quality or the haircut level agreed. The repricing right is a structural protection that is independent of, and complementary to, the haircut and margin maintenance provisions.
151: Any counterparty that deletes the repricing right entirely, or that confines the repricing right to maturity rolls only (effectively eliminating intra-term repricing), is proposing a position that falls outside Voss Bank's risk tolerance. The desk should not agree to such a proposal, even as a concession in exchange for favourable terms on other points.
152: In the Meridian negotiation, Meridian's Turn 2 redline effectively deleted repricing for in-term periods by proposing that repricing be available only at maturity roll — that is, only when the original Transaction matures and the parties agree to roll the trade into a new Transaction. This was flagged as unacceptable by Calder Stone Partners LLP, and Alistair Fenn communicated a revised Voss Bank position to PAG by email on 4 April 2025. The revised position — 90th day or quarterly, whichever is later, with 2 business days' notice — is within the acceptable range and should be accepted by Meridian at Turn 3.
153: If Meridian continues to resist the repricing right at Turn 3, the desk should escalate to Henrik J. Lindqvist for a direct conversation with Dana R. Castellano. The repricing right is a non-negotiable structural protection, and Voss Bank will not proceed with the Meridian GMRA without it.
154: Section 8 — Cross-Default Threshold
155: 8.1 — Preferred Position
156: Voss Bank's preferred cross-default threshold is $10,000,000 (ten million US dollars). This represents the minimum amount of third-party indebtedness that, if subject to default, acceleration, or non-payment at maturity, triggers a cross-default Event of Default under the GMRA. The cross-default threshold applies to both parties (Buyer and Seller) and is intended to provide early warning of a counterparty's financial distress by capturing defaults on material third-party obligations.
157: A low cross-default threshold is consistent with Voss Bank's conservative credit risk management philosophy. By setting the threshold at $10,000,000, Voss Bank ensures that relatively small defaults on third-party indebtedness — which may be precursors to broader financial difficulty — trigger the GMRA's Event of Default provisions and enable Voss Bank to exercise its close-out and liquidation rights before the counterparty's financial position deteriorates further.
158: 8.2 — Acceptable Range
159: Voss Bank's acceptable range for the cross-default threshold is $10,000,000 to $25,000,000. Within this range, the desk may agree any figure without escalation to the Credit Committee.
160: The following considerations should inform the desk's calibration of the cross-default threshold within the acceptable range:
161: •  Counterparty's net capital or regulatory capital. A threshold of approximately 5–7% of audited net capital is a reasonable benchmark that ensures the cross-default provision is triggered by defaults that are material relative to the counterparty's financial resources, without being so low as to capture trivial or operational payment failures. For Meridian Capital Securities LLC (audited net capital of $412,000,000 as at 31 December 2024), a $25,000,000 threshold represents approximately 6.07% of net capital, which falls within the 5–7% benchmark range.
162: •  Nature of the counterparty's other financial indebtedness. Counterparties with large outstanding bond or loan portfolios may argue that a low cross-default threshold creates an unacceptable risk of a cascade of cross-acceleration events — where a default under one agreement triggers cross-defaults under multiple other agreements, amplifying financial distress rather than providing early warning. This concern has some merit, and the desk should be prepared to move within the acceptable range to accommodate it.
163: •  Likelihood of cross-acceleration cascades. In markets subject to stress, a low cross-default threshold can itself contribute to systemic instability by triggering a chain of cross-defaults across multiple master agreements. The desk should consider whether the counterparty's overall cross-default architecture (across its ISDA Master Agreements, GMRAs, prime brokerage agreements, and other trading documentation) is consistent with the threshold proposed under this GMRA.
164: 8.3 — Walk-Away
165: Any cross-default threshold above $50,000,000 is a walk-away. At that level, the cross-default provision becomes commercially meaningless for a counterparty of Meridian's size and profile — a $50,000,000 default would represent only approximately 12.1% of Meridian's net capital, and a counterparty in that degree of distress would likely already have triggered other Events of Default (e.g., failure to pay, Act of Insolvency) before the cross-default threshold was reached.
166: Thresholds between $25,000,001 and $50,000,000 fall within the escalation band. The desk does not have authority to agree a threshold in this range without Credit Committee approval. The Credit Committee will assess whether the higher threshold is justified by the counterparty's credit profile, the nature of the trading relationship, and any risk-mitigating factors (e.g., the availability of additional collateral, the existence of a credit support annex, or the counterparty's agreement to enhanced reporting obligations).
167: 8.4 — Meridian Negotiation Status
168: The cross-default threshold is one of the open commercial issues in the Meridian negotiation. The negotiation history is as follows:
169: •  Voss Bank's Turn 1 and Turn 2 position: $10,000,000.
170: •  Meridian's Turn 2 counter: $50,000,000 (at the walk-away boundary).
171: •  Expected Meridian Turn 3 counter: $25,000,000 (the top of Voss Bank's acceptable range).
172: If Meridian comes back at $25,000,000 in its Turn 3 redline, the desk is authorised to agree without escalation. This figure represents 6.07% of Meridian's audited net capital, which falls within the 5–7% benchmark range and is consistent with the cross-default thresholds agreed in comparable GMRA negotiations with US broker-dealers of similar size and credit profile.
173: If Meridian holds at $50,000,000 or proposes a figure between $25,000,001 and $50,000,000, the desk must escalate to the Credit Committee pursuant to Section 12.
174: Section 9 — Act of Insolvency Grace Period
175: 9.1 — Preferred Position
176: Voss Bank's preferred position is zero days — any Act of Insolvency constitutes an immediate Event of Default with no cure or grace period. An Act of Insolvency is defined in the GMRA to include (among other things) the presentation of a winding-up petition, the appointment of an administrator, receiver, or trustee, the filing of a voluntary bankruptcy petition, and any analogous proceeding under the laws of the relevant jurisdiction.
177: The zero-day position reflects Voss Bank's view that any Act of Insolvency — even a technical or involuntary filing — creates an immediate and material risk to Voss Bank's ability to realise its collateral rights and to enforce close-out netting. In the US context, the commencement of SIPA proceedings against a broker-dealer can result in an immediate freeze on the firm's assets and trading activity, and any delay in triggering the GMRA's Event of Default provisions increases the risk that Voss Bank will be unable to close out its positions and liquidate collateral before the counterparty's assets are placed beyond reach.
178: The desk should be aware that the zero-day position will meet resistance from virtually all counterparties, and particularly from US broker-dealers, which will argue that involuntary filings (e.g., creditor-initiated winding-up petitions) should not trigger an immediate Event of Default because such filings may be frivolous or may be dismissed before any insolvency proceeding is actually commenced. This is a valid concern, and the desk should be prepared to move within the acceptable range described below.
179: 9.2 — Acceptable Range
180: Voss Bank may agree a grace period of up to 15 business days without Credit Committee escalation. Within this range, the desk should seek the shortest period the counterparty will accept. Typical negotiated outcomes fall between 5 and 15 business days, depending on the counterparty's regulatory status, the nature of the insolvency events covered, and the counterparty's negotiating leverage.
181: The following considerations are relevant when calibrating the grace period within the acceptable range:
182: •  Involuntary proceedings only. Some counterparties will request a grace period only for involuntary insolvency proceedings (e.g., creditor-initiated winding-up petitions) while accepting an immediate Event of Default for voluntary proceedings (e.g., the counterparty's own filing for bankruptcy protection). This is a reasonable distinction, and the desk may agree a bifurcated grace period structure — zero days for voluntary Acts of Insolvency, and up to 15 business days for involuntary Acts of Insolvency — without escalation.
183: •  Dismissal condition. The grace period should be conditional on the relevant insolvency proceeding being dismissed or stayed within the grace period. If the proceeding is not dismissed or stayed within the grace period, the Act of Insolvency constitutes an Event of Default at the expiry of the grace period without further notice or action by Voss Bank. The desk should resist counterparty proposals that extend the grace period indefinitely or that require Voss Bank to demonstrate prejudice before triggering the Event of Default.
184: •  Notice requirement. It is acceptable for the grace period to begin running from the date on which the Defaulting Party (i.e., the counterparty) gives notice of the Act of Insolvency to the Non-Defaulting Party (i.e., Voss Bank), rather than from the date of the Act of Insolvency itself. This ensures that the grace period does not expire before Voss Bank becomes aware of the insolvency event. However, the desk should insist that the Defaulting Party has an affirmative obligation to notify the Non-Defaulting Party prrace periods between 16 and 20 business days. Note: above 20 business days is a firm walk-away regardless of Credit Committee view.
245: (f) Any deviation from English governing law. This is both an escalation trigger and a walk-away; the Credit Committee may consider the matter but is not expected to approve any deviation from English law.
246: (g) Any modification to the Net Exposure Cap set by the Credit Committee for a specific counterparty. The Net Exposure Cap is a Credit Committee-set parameter; the desk does not have authority to modify it, even within a narrow range.
247: (h) Acceptance of exclusive court jurisdiction (of any court, in any jurisdiction).
248: (i) Any non-standard netting, set-off, or close-out netting provisions — including any provisions that modify the close-out netting mechanics of Paragraph 10 of the GMRA, any provisions that introduce a set-off right that is broader than the GMRA's standard set-off provisions, or any provisions that restrict the Non-Defaulting Party's right to calculate a Default Market Value.
249: This list is not exhaustive. If the desk encounters a counterparty proposal on any term not specifically addressed in this playbook, and the desk is uncertain whether the proposal falls within its delegated authority, the desk should err on the side of escalation.
250: 12.2 — Escalation Procedure
251: The escalation procedure is as follows:
252: 1.  The desk lead (currently Henrik J. Lindqvist for the London Branch) prepares a one-page deviation memorandum setting out:
253: (a) the Voss Bank preferred position on the relevant term;
254: (b) the counterparty's proposal, including the specific language proposed (with a redline against the Voss Bank position where applicable);
255: (c) the commercial rationale for the deviation — i.e., why the counterparty is insisting on a position outside the acceptable range, and whether there are offsetting commercial benefits (e.g., improved pricing, higher volumes, or concessions on other terms);
256: (d) any risk-mitigating conditions proposed — i.e., additional protections that Voss Bank could negotiate to offset the increased risk of the deviation (e.g., a lower Net Exposure Cap, enhanced reporting obligations, additional collateral requirements, or a shorter tenor limit).
257: 2.  The memorandum is submitted to the Credit Committee via the Zürich Legal Coordination inbox (legalcoord@vossbank.ch). The memorandum should be marked "GMRA Deviation — [Counterparty Name] — [Term]" in the subject line.
258: 3.  Target turnaround: 3 business days for standard deviations; 1 business day for time-sensitive negotiations (e.g., where a Turn deadline is imminent or where the counterparty has set a deadline for commercial agreement). If the desk requires expedited turnaround, this should be noted in the subject line of the submission email.
259: 4.  The Credit Committee will respond with one of three decisions: (i) approved as proposed; (ii) approved with conditions (specifying risk-mitigating conditions that must be incorporated into the GMRA); or (iii) declined (in which case the desk must revert to the preferred position or the nearest acceptable position within the playbook range).
260: 12.3 — Authority Levels
261: The following table summarises the authority framework:
263: For the avoidance of doubt, the walk-away thresholds identified in this playbook are absolute limits on the authority of both the desk and the Credit Committee. Neither the desk nor the Credit Committee may approve a term that is at or beyond a walk-away threshold, except where this playbook expressly states that the Credit Committee retains residual discretion (which is the case only for Act of Insolvency grace periods between 16 and 20 business days, as noted in Section 9.3).
264: Section 13 — Income Payments
265: 13.1 — Standard Position
266: Manufactured Payments on Purchased Securities — that is, payments by the Buyer to the Seller equal to the income (e.g., coupon payments, interest distributions) that the Seller would have received on the Purchased Securities had those securities not been transferred to the Buyer — are due on the next business day following the record date for the relevant income payment.
267: This timing convention ensures that the manufactured payment is made promptly after the record date, without the settlement risk that would arise if the payment were aligned with the actual distribution date (which may fall on a weekend, public holiday, or non-business day in the relevant settlement system).
268: 13.2 — Negotiation Guidance
269: The desk should resist counterparty attempts to align manufactured payment dates with actual payment dates (which may fall on non-business days and create settlement risk). The "next business day following the record date" convention is standard market practice for GMRA manufactured payments and should not be controversial with most counterparties.
270: If a counterparty proposes an alternative timing convention — for example, manufactured payments due on the actual payment date, or manufactured payments due on the second business day following the record date — the desk should explain that the standard convention is designed to minimise settlement risk and operational complexity, and should insist on the standard position.
271: The desk should also ensure that the GMRA clearly specifies the obligations of both parties with respect to manufactured payments in the context of a margin transfer. If Margin Securities have been delivered, the obligation to make manufactured payments on those Margin Securities should be addressed separately from the obligation to make manufactured payments on Purchased Securities.
272: Section 14 — Settlement Systems
273: 14.1 — Standard Elections
274: The following settlement systems are the standard elections for all GMRA negotiations conducted by the London Branch:
276: These elections reflect the London Branch's existing settlement infrastructure and custodian relationships. Collateral denominated in other currencies (e.g., GBP, JPY, CAD) is not a standard offering under the London Branch's current GMRA programme; if a counterparty proposes non-EUR, non-USD collateral, the desk must consult Operations (London) to confirm whether settlement capability exists for the relevant currency and settlement system before agreeing to include such collateral in the Eligible Collateral definition.
277: 14.2 — Tri-Party Option
278: Where a tri-party structure is elected for one or more Transactions, Voss Bank's approved tri-party custodian is BNY Meliora Trust Company, N.A. The selection of BNY Meliora reflects the London Branch's existing tri-party custodian relationship and the Branch's familiarity with BNY Meliora's collateral management platform, eligible securities schedules, and operational procedures.
279: Tri-party is not the default structure under this playbook. The standard structure is bilateral settlement, in which collateral moves directly between the parties' accounts at Clearstream or DTC without the intermediation of a tri-party custodian. Tri-party is elected only where specifically agreed between the parties and documented via a separate tri-party annexe (appended to the GMRA) and a tri-party custodian agreement (entered into among the parties and BNY Meliora).
280: The desk should note that the tri-party structure introduces additional documentation requirements, including the negotiation of the tri-party annexe, the tri-party custodian agreement, and the eligible securities schedule. These documents are typically negotiated in parallel with the GMRA itself and may involve separate negotiations with BNY Meliora's documentation team. If tri-party is contemplated, the desk should notify Legal and Operations as early as possible in the negotiation process to allow sufficient time for the parallel documentation workstream.
281: Section 15 — FINMA Regulatory Requirements
282: 15.1 — Close-Out Netting Opinions
283: Prior to executing any GMRA, Legal must confirm that a current (within 12 months) enforceability opinion on close-out netting under the laws of the counterparty's jurisdiction is on file. The opinion must be provided by a law firm approved by Voss Bank's Chief Legal Officer and must cover the following matters:
284: •  The enforceability of the GMRA's close-out netting provisions (Paragraph 10) under the laws of the counterparty's jurisdiction of organisation.
285: •  The enforceability of close-out netting in the event of the counterparty's insolvency, including any applicable insolvency safe harbours or exemptions.
286: •  For US counterparties, the opinion must specifically address SIPA/SIPC treatment of repo collateral and the enforceability of netting under the US Bankruptcy Code safe harbours (11 U.S.C. §§ 559, 561, and related provisions). The opinion must confirm that repo transactions under the GMRA qualify as "repurchase agreements" for the purposes of the Bankruptcy Code safe harbours and that the Non-Defaulting Party's contractual right to liquidate, terminate, or accelerate is protected from the automatic stay.
287: The netting opinion must be refreshed at least annually (i.e., a new opinion must be obtained within 12 months of the date of the most recent opinion). If a netting opinion is more than 12 months old at the time of execution of a new GMRA or at the time of entry into a new Transaction under an existing GMRA, the desk must not proceed until a refreshed opinion is obtained.
288: Legal maintains a register of all netting opinions on file, including the jurisdiction, the date of the opinion, the opining law firm, and the expiry date. The desk should check this register before commencing any new GMRA negotiation.
289: 15.2 — Capital Treatment
290: The GMRA must include terms sufficient to ensure that reverse repo transactions qualify for securities financing transaction (SFT) treatment under the Basel III framework as implemented by FINMA (Capital Adequacy Ordinance (CAO), Art. 56 et seq.). SFT treatment allows Voss Bank to recognise the collateral received under reverse repo transactions for the purposes of calculating credit risk-weighted assets and leverage ratio exposure, subject to compliance with the applicable eligibility conditions.
291: Key conditions for SFT treatment include:
292: •  The GMRA must provide for enforceable close-out netting (see Section 15.1).
293: •  The collateral must be revalued at least daily (which is ensured by the GMRA's standard margin maintenance provisions).
294: •  The collateral must be liquid and must not exhibit a material positive correlation with the credit quality of the counterparty (this is ensured by the Eligible Collateral criteria set out in Section 3).
295: Haircuts below HQLA floors (see Section 3.3) may cause the transaction to attract higher capital charges under the standardised approach supervisory haircut framework. If haircuts approach the HQLA floors, the desk must escalate to Treasury (Zürich) to confirm the capital impact before agreeing the haircut level.
296: 15.3 — Large Exposure Reporting
297: Aggregate gross exposure to a single counterparty under the GMRA must be monitored against FINMA large exposure limits. Under the FINMA framework, a bank's total exposure to a single counterparty (or group of connected counterparties) may not exceed 25% of the bank's eligible capital (Tier 1 capital plus Tier 2 capital, subject to applicable limits).
298: The Net Exposure Cap set by the Credit Committee for each counterparty is designed to remain well within the FINMA large exposure limit, providing a buffer against fluctuations in exposure due to market movements, new trades, or collateral value changes. The desk should be aware that the Net Exposure Cap is not the same as the large exposure limit — the Cap is typically set at a level significantly below the regulatory limit to allow headroom for operational and market-driven exposure increases.
299: If the aggregate gross exposure to a counterparty under the GMRA approaches the Net Exposure Cap, or if the desk becomes aware of circumstances that could cause the aggregate exposure to exceed the FINMA large exposure limit (including exposure under other master agreements, such as the ISDA Master Agreement), the desk must immediately notify Risk Management (Zürich) and the Credit Committee.
300: Section 16 — Non-Commercial Drafting Mark-Ups
301: 16.1 — General Approach
302: In any GMRA negotiation, the counterparty's counsel will typically propose a number of non-commercial drafting mark-ups in addition to the substantive commercial and legal proposals addressed in the preceding sections. Non-commercial mark-ups include, without limitation:
303: •  Clarifications to defined terms that do not alter commercial substance.
304: •  Conforming changes to ensure internal consistency within the GMRA and Annex I.
305: •  Typographical corrections.
306: •  Notice mechanic refinements (e.g., updating notice addresses, adding email as a permitted notice method, adjusting deemed-receipt provisions).
307: •  Cross-referencing corrections.
308: •  Grammatical and stylistic changes.
309: These non-commercial mark-ups should be assessed on their merits. While they do not typically raise commercial or risk concerns, they may inadvertently alter the legal effect of a provision if not reviewed carefully. Accordingly, all non-commercial mark-ups are reviewed by Calder Stone Partners LLP before being accepted or rejected by the desk.
310: Where Calder Stone confirms that a mark-up is purely clarificatory and does not alter commercial substance, the desk may accept the mark-up without escalation to the Credit Committee. Where Calder Stone identifies a mark-up that appears non-commercial but may have unintended commercial or legal consequences, the mark-up is treated as a substantive proposal and is addressed through the relevant section of this playbook.
311: In the Meridian negotiation, 16 of 23 total Turn 2 mark-ups were classified as non-commercial. Of the 14 marks addressed in the Fenn email of 4 April 2025, 7 were accepted (all of which were non-commercial). The remaining 9 unaddressed marks are pending Voss Bank Credit Committee review. Of these 9 unaddressed marks, the desk expects that a number will be reclassified as non-commercial upon further review, with the remainder being addressed as substantive issues in the Turn 3 redline.
312: Section 17 — Counterparty-Specific Notes: Meridian Capital Securities LLC
313: This section consolidates all counterparty-specific information, issues tracking, and Annex I elections relevant to the ongoing GMRA negotiation with Meridian Capital Securities LLC. It is intended to serve as a quick-reference summary for the desk and Legal, and supplements (but does not replace) the detailed guidance on each term set out in Sections 2–16 of this playbook.
314: 17.1 — Counterparty Profile
316: Meridian is a mid-tier US broker-dealer with a diversified secured funding business, including significant activity in US Treasury repo, agency MBS repo, and investment-grade corporate repo. Meridian is a member of FINRA and is registered with the SEC under Section 15 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Meridian is also a member of SIPC.
317: Voss Bank's external counsel for the Meridian negotiation is Calder Stone Partners LLP, with Alistair Fenn (Partner) and Sana K. Abboud (Associate) acting as the primary contacts. Calder Stone's role includes reviewing and responding to all Meridian mark-ups, advising on English-law enforceability issues, and attending negotiation calls as required.
318: 17.2 — Negotiation Timeline
320: 17.3 — Issues Resolution Tracker
321: The following table tracks the status of all substantive commercial and legal issues in the Meridian negotiation. Issues are numbered sequentially for ease of reference.
323: 17.4 — Substitution (Resolved)
324: The substitution issue was resolved between the parties as follows:
325: •  Agreed framework: No Buyer consent required, subject to three conditions: (i) 1 business day's prior notice to the Buyer; (ii) substitute collateral must be of the same or better Eligible Collateral category; and (iii) no outstanding Margin Deficit at the time of substitution.
326: •  Resolution process: Alistair Fenn (Calder Stone) proposed this framework to Rachel S. Okonkwo (PAG) by email on 4 April 2025. Okonkwo confirmed Meridian's acceptance of the framework by email on 14 April 2025.
327: •  Playbook status: This resolution is within the acceptable fallback stated in Section 6.2 and did not require escalation.
329: 17.5 — Voss Bank Annex I Elections Summary (Meridian)
330: The following table summarises the Annex I elections for the Meridian GMRA, reflecting both the standard playbook positions and the counterparty-specific terms agreed to date. Elections for open issues are shown in their expected final form, subject to confirmation upon receipt of Meridian's Turn 3 redline.
332: Section 18 — Document Version History
334: Section 19 — Confidentiality Notice
335: This document is the proprietary and confidential work product of Voss Bank AG. It is intended solely for use by authorised personnel of the Collateral Trading & Legal team at the London Branch and at the Zürich head office, and by members of the Credit Committee (Zürich) who are authorised to receive it under the distribution list set out on the cover page of this document.
336: This document must not be shared with, or disclosed to, any counterparty, counterparty counsel, broker, intermediary, regulatory authority (except upon formal regulatory request in accordance with Voss Bank's regulatory engagement policy), or any other third party. Unauthorised disclosure may constitute a breach of Voss Bank's internal compliance policies, the terms of engagement with Calder Stone Partners LLP, and applicable regulatory obligations, including the FCA's requirements on the management of confidential information.
337: This document contains negotiation positions, approved fallback terms, and walk-away thresholds that, if disclosed to a counterparty, would materially prejudice Voss Bank's negotiating position in current and future GMRA negotiations. All recipients of this document are reminded of their obligations under Voss Bank's Information Security Policy and their personal responsibility to safeguard confidential business information.

015: Paragraph 1 — Applicability

016: 1.1 This Agreement is a Global Master Repurchase Agreement in the form published by the International Capital Market Association in 2011 (the "2011 ICMA GMRA"), as supplemented by Annex I (Supplemental Terms and Conditions) in the form published by ICMA in 2011 (the "2011 Annex I") and by Annex II (Elections, Supplements, and Amendments) attached hereto .

017: 1.2 This Agreement, together with Annex I, Annex II, each Confirmation exchanged between the parties, and any other schedules, appendices, or annexes expressly incorporated herein by reference, shall together constitute a single agreement between Buyer and Seller (collectively, the "Agreement"). Each of the parties acknowledges that all Transactions entered into on or after the date of this Agreement are entered into in reliance on the fact that this Agreement, Annex I, Annex II, and all Confirmations form a single agreement between the parties.

018: 1.3 Each Transaction entered into between the parties on or after the date of this Agreement shall be governed by and subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. In the event of any inconsistency between the provisions of the body of this Agreement and the provisions of Annex I or Annex II, the provisions of Annex II shall prevail, followed by the provisions of Annex I, and then by the provisions of the body of this Agreement.

019: 1.4 Buy/Sell Back Transactions: Not Applicable. The parties do not intend to enter into Buy/Sell Back Transactions under this Agreement. If the parties wish to enter into Buy/Sell Back Transactions, they shall negotiate and agree a separate annex or amendment to this Agreement addressing such Transactions.

020: 1.5 Agency Transactions: Not Applicable. Neither party acts as agent for any third party in connection with any Transaction entered into under this Agreement. If the parties wish to enter into Agency Transactions, they shall negotiate and agree a separate annex or amendment to this Agreement addressing such Transactions.
021: Paragraph 2 — Definitions

022: 2.1 Unless otherwise defined in this Agreement or the context otherwise requires, capitalised terms used in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the 2011 ICMA GMRA and the 2011 Annex I, which definitions are hereby incorporated by reference as if set out in full herein.

023: 2.2 In addition to the definitions set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA and the 2011 Annex I, the following additional defined terms are introduced in Annex II and, to the extent set out therein, shall apply for the purposes of this Agreement:
024: (a) "Eligible Collateral" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 3(c).
025: (b) "Eligible Sovereign Securities" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 3(a).
026: (c) "Eligible Corporate Securities" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 3(b).
027: (d) "Haircut" or "Haircut Percentage" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 4.
028: (e) "Margin Threshold" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 5.
029: (f) "Net Exposure Cap" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 6.
031:   "Cross-Default Threshold" has the meaning given in Annex II, Section 10(c).
032:   "Act of Insolvency Grace Period"   Annex II, Section 11(b).

034: 2.3 In the event of any inconsistency between a definition contained in Annex II and a definition of the same term contained in the body of this Agreement, the 2011 ICMA GMRA, or the 2011 Annex I, the definition in Annex II shall prevail.

035: 2.4 "Base Currency" means United States Dollars (USD). All calculations of Transaction Exposure, Margin Deficit, Margin Excess, Net Exposure, and all other amounts required to be computed in a single currency under this Agreement shall be calculated in, or converted into, the Base Currency at the spot rate of exchange prevailing at the relevant time of determination, as reasonably determined by Buyer.

036: 2.5 "Business Day" means a day (other than a Saturday or Sunday) on which commercial banks are open for general business (including dealings in foreign exchange and foreign currency deposits) in both London, England and New York, New York, United States of America.
037: 2.6 For the avoidance of doubt, where any term is defined in both this Paragraph 2 and in Annex II, the Annex II definition shall govern.
039: Paragraph 3 — Initiation; Confirmations

040: 3.1 Each Transaction shall be entered into by telephone, electronic messaging (including Bloomberg messaging, SWIFT, or electronic mail), or such other method as may be agreed between the parties from time to time. Each party shall designate one or more authorised persons who shall have authority to enter into Transactions on its behalf, and each party shall provide the other with a written list of such authorised persons, updated from time to time as necessary.

041: 3.2 Each Transaction shall be evidenced by a Confirmation in writing delivered by Buyer or Seller (as agreed between the parties for such purpose) by close of business on the Business Day following the Purchase Date. A Confirmation may be delivered by electronic mail, facsimile, or through an electronic trade confirmation platform used by both parties. Each party shall use reasonable efforts to respond promptly to any Confirmation received and to notify the other party of any discrepancy in the terms set out therein.
042: 3.3 The Confirmation for each Transaction shall specify, at a minimum, the following:
043: (a) the Purchase Date;
044: (b) the Repurchase Date, or, if the Transaction is an open Transaction or an "on demand" Transaction, a statement to that effect;

045: (c) the Purchased Securities, including the International Securities Identification Number (ISIN), the nominal amount or face value, and a description (including issuer name, coupon rate, and maturity date) of such securities;
046: (d) the Purchase Price;
047: (e) the Repurchase Price or, alternatively, the Pricing Rate and the basis for computation of the Repurchase Price;
048: (f) Buyer's account details for the receipt of Purchased Securities and for the payment of the Purchase Price;
049: (g) Seller's account details for the delivery of Purchased Securities and for the receipt of the Purchase Price;
050: (h) the applicable Haircut Percentage;

051: (i) any additional terms specifically agreed between the parties for that Transaction, including any special conditions, additional collateral requirements, or modifications to the standard terms of this Agreement applicable solely to that Transaction.

052: 3.4 A Confirmation shall, upon delivery, supplement, form part of, and be subject to this Agreement. Together with this Agreement, each Confirmation shall evidence a complete and binding agreement between the parties with respect to the Transaction to which it relates. In the event of any inconsistency between the terms of a Confirmation and the terms of this Agreement (including Annex I and Annex II), the terms of the Confirmation shall prevail with respect to the Transaction to which such Confirmation relates, unless the Confirmation expressly provides otherwise.

053: 3.5 The failure by either party to deliver a Confirmation with respect to a Transaction shall not affect the validity or enforceability of that Transaction, provided that the terms thereof have been agreed between the parties.
055: Paragraph 4 — Margin Maintenance
056: Paragraph 4(a) — Margin Deficit / Margin Excess

057: 4.1 The parties shall, on each Business Day (or at such other intervals as may be agreed), mark to market all outstanding Transactions by reference to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities and the Transaction Exposure in respect of each Transaction, each calculated in the Base Currency.

058: 4.2 If at any time the aggregate Cash Margin (if any) held by or on behalf of Buyer, together with the aggregate Market Value of all Purchased Securities held by Buyer (adjusted by the application of the relevant Haircut Percentage), is less than the aggregate Transaction Exposure of Buyer with respect to all Transactions then outstanding, a "Margin Deficit" shall be deemed to exist. The amount of such Margin Deficit shall be equal to the shortfall, calculated in the Base Currency.

059: 4.3 If at any time the aggregate Market Value of all Purchased Securities held by Buyer (adjusted by the application of the relevant Haircut Percentage), together with any Cash Margin held by or on behalf of Buyer, exceeds the aggregate Transaction Exposure of Buyer with respect to all Transactions then outstanding, a "Margin Excess" shall be deemed to exist. The amount of such Margin Excess shall be equal to the surplus, calculated in the Base Currency.
060: Paragraph 4(b) — Delivery Amount / Return Amount

061: 4.4 Upon the existence of a Margin Deficit, Buyer may by notice to Seller (a "Margin Call") require Seller to transfer to Buyer Additional Purchased Securities or Cash Margin (or any combination thereof) in an amount sufficient to eliminate such Margin Deficit (the aggregate amount so required, the "Delivery Amount"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no transfer shall be required if the Delivery Amount would be less than or equal to the applicable Margin Threshold specified in Annex II, Section 5(a) (being   as of the date hereof).

062: 4.5 Upon the existence of a Margin Excess, Seller may by notice to Buyer (also a "Margin Call") require Buyer to transfer to Seller Equivalent Securities or Cash Margin (or any combination thereof) sufficient to eliminate such Margin Excess (the aggregate amount so required, the "Return Amount"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no transfer shall be required if the Return Amount would be less than or equal to the applicable Margin Threshold specified in Annex II, Section 5(b) (being   as of the date hereof).

063: 4.6 Any Additional Purchased Securities transferred by Seller to Buyer pursuant to a Margin Call must constitute Eligible Collateral, and the Market Value of such Additional Purchased Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) shall be at least equal to the Delivery Amount.
064: Paragraph 4(c) — Margin Call Timing

065: 4.7 A Margin Call must be received by the other party by the margin call cut-off time specified in Annex II, Section 7 (being 10:00 a.m. London time as of the date hereof) in order for the resulting transfer to be required on that same Business Day.
066: 4.8 If a Margin Call is received before the cut-off time on a Business Day, the party receiving the Margin Call shall make the required transfer on that same Business Day.

067: 4.9 If a Margin Call is received at or after the cut-off time on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the party receiving the Margin Call shall make the required transfer on the next following Business Day.

068: 4.10 For the purposes of this Paragraph 4(c), a Margin Call shall be deemed to have been "received" when it is actually received by the recipient at the address, facsimile number, or electronic mail address specified in Annex II, Section 14 for the giving of notices. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to acknowledge receipt of a Margin Call promptly upon receipt.
069: Paragraph 4(d) — Haircuts
070: 4.11 The applicable Haircut Percentage for each category of Eligible Collateral is as specified in Annex II, Section 4, and is summarised as follows:

072: 4.12 The Transaction Exposure in respect of any Transaction shall be calculated by applying the relevant Haircut Percentage to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities. The Haircut Percentage shall be applied in the manner set out in Annex II, Section 4, such that the Purchase Price for a Transaction shall be determined by dividing the Market Value of the Purchased Securities by one (1) plus the applicable Haircut Percentage (expressed as a decimal).

073: 4.13 Buyer reserves the right, upon not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to Seller, to revise the applicable Haircut Percentage for any category of Eligible Collateral in connection with future Transactions, provided that (a) any such revision shall apply only to Transactions entered into after the effective date of such revision and shall not affect the terms of any Transaction already outstanding, and (b) any such revision shall be made in good faith and on a commercially reasonable basis, having regard to prevailing market conditions, the credit quality of the relevant class of securities, and Buyer's internal risk management policies.
074: Paragraph 5 — Income Payments

075: 5.1 Where Purchased Securities are held by Buyer on a record date, ex-dividend date, or other relevant date for any distribution of Income (including, without limitation, any coupon, interest payment, dividend, principal repayment (other than at maturity), or other distribution payable in respect of such Purchased Securities), Buyer shall, on the next Business Day following the date on which Buyer receives or is credited with such Income, pay to Seller an amount equal to such Income (a "Manufactured Payment").

076: 5.2 Manufactured Payments shall be made in the currency in which the relevant Income payment is denominated and shall be paid to the account designated by Seller for the receipt of funds in such currency, as specified in the relevant Confirmation or as otherwise notified by Seller to Buyer in writing.

077: 5.3 All Manufactured Payments shall be made net of any applicable withholding tax, deduction, or other amount required to be withheld or deducted by Buyer under applicable law. If Buyer is required by applicable law to make any such withholding or deduction, the provisions of Paragraph 11 (Tax) shall apply with respect to any obligation of Buyer to gross up such payment.

078: 5.4 For the avoidance of doubt, the obligation to make a Manufactured Payment arises regardless of whether Buyer has actually received the relevant Income payment from the issuer of the Purchased Securities. Buyer's obligation to make the Manufactured Payment is an independent obligation under this Agreement and shall not be conditional upon Buyer's receipt of the underlying Income.
080: Paragraph 6 — Payment and Transfer
081: Paragraph 6(a) — Method

082: 6.1 All payments of cash required to be made under this Agreement shall be made in immediately available, freely transferable, same-day funds in the relevant currency to the account specified by the receiving party in the relevant Confirmation, in Annex II, Section 14, or as otherwise notified by the receiving party to the paying party in writing from time to time.

083: 6.2 All transfers of Securities required to be made under this Agreement (including the initial transfer of Purchased Securities, the transfer of Additional Purchased Securities, the return of Equivalent Securities, and the transfer of Alternative Securities upon substitution) shall be made through the applicable settlement system, as follows:
084: (a) For Euro-denominated Eligible Collateral: Clearstream Banking S.A., in accordance with the rules and procedures of Clearstream Banking S.A. as in effect from time to time.
085: (b) For USD-denominated Eligible Collateral: The Depository Trust Company (DTC), in accordance with the rules and procedures of DTC as in effect from time to time.

086: 6.3 Each party shall bear its own costs and expenses in connection with the settlement of Securities through the applicable settlement system, including any fees or charges imposed by the settlement system operator, the relevant custodian, or any intermediary in the settlement chain, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties.

087: 6.4 Unless otherwise agreed between the parties for a specific Transaction, all deliveries of Securities shall be made on a delivery-versus-payment (DvP) basis. If DvP settlement is not available or practicable for a particular Transaction, the parties shall agree in advance on an alternative delivery mechanism and shall cooperate in good faith to minimise settlement risk.
088: Paragraph 6(b) — Netting

089: 6.5 As elected in Annex II, Section 8, Paragraph 7(b) of this Agreement (settlement netting for obligations in the same currency falling due on the same settlement date) shall apply. The parties agree that, where on any Business Day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and on the same settlement date by each party to the other (whether under Paragraph 4, Paragraph 5, or otherwise under this Agreement), such obligations shall be subject to the netting provisions set out in Paragraph 7 below.
090: Paragraph 7 — Netting of Obligations
091: Paragraph 7(a) — Payment Netting

092: 7.1 The standard payment netting provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. Accordingly, where on any Business Day amounts would be payable by each party to the other in the same currency and on the same value date, the mutual obligations of each party to make any such payment shall be automatically satisfied and discharged and replaced by an obligation upon the party by whom the larger aggregate amount would have been payable to pay to the other party the excess of the larger aggregate amount over the smaller aggregate amount. Such single net payment shall be made by the party owing the net amount on the relevant value date in the manner specified in Paragraph 6(a).
093: Paragraph 7(b) — Close-out Netting / Settlement Netting

094: 7.2 Elected. If on any day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and in respect of the same settlement date by each party to the other (whether pursuant to Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance), Paragraph 5 (Income Payments), Paragraph 10 (Events of Default), or otherwise under this Agreement), the obligations of each party to make any such payment shall be automatically satisfied and discharged and, if the aggregate amount payable by one party exceeds the aggregate amount payable by the other party, replaced by an obligation upon the party by whom the larger aggregate amount would have been payable to pay to the other party the excess of the larger aggregate amount over the smaller aggregate amount.

095: 7.3 The single net amount determined in accordance with Paragraph 7.2 above shall be payable in the relevant currency on the relevant settlement date, and only the net amount shall be required to be paid by the party owing such amount. The other party shall have no obligation to make any payment in respect of the amounts so netted.

096: 7.4 Each party represents that the netting provisions of this Paragraph 7 are enforceable against it in all relevant jurisdictions, including the jurisdiction of its incorporation or organisation, the jurisdiction of its principal office, and any other jurisdiction in which it conducts business or holds assets. Each party agrees to take such steps and execute such documents as may reasonably be required to give effect to the netting provisions of this Paragraph 7.
097: Paragraph 8 — Substitution

098: 8.1 Subject to the provisions of Annex II, Section 9, Seller may from time to time during the term of any Transaction   of Alternative Securities for all or any part of the Purchased Securities in that Transaction.

099: 8.2 Any   shall be made by Seller to Buyer in writing (including by electronic mail) and shall specify the Purchased Securities to be replaced, the proposed Alternative Securities, and the proposed date on which the substitution is to take effect. The   shall include sufficient detail regarding the proposed Alternative Securities (including ISIN, nominal amount, issuer, coupon, maturity, and credit rating) to enable Buyer to evaluate the  .

102: 8.4   substitution shall be effected on the Business Day   by the simultaneous transfer of the Alternative Securities by Seller to Buyer (or to Buyer's account at the relevant settlement system) and the transfer of the relevant Purchased Securities by Buyer to Seller (or to Seller's account at the relevant settlement system), in each case in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 6.
103: 8.5 Any Alternative Securities transferred by Seller must qualify as Eligible Collateral and must satisfy all of the eligibility criteria set out in Annex II, Section 3.

104: 8.6 Upon completion of a substitution, the Alternative Securities shall become the Purchased Securities for all purposes of the relevant Transaction, and the Confirmation for such Transaction shall be deemed to have been amended accordingly.
105: Paragraph 9 — Representations
106: 9.1 Each party represents and warrants to the other, as of the date of this Agreement and as of each Purchase Date on which it enters into a Transaction, that:

107: (a) Due Organisation and Authority. It is duly organised, validly existing, and in good standing (or the equivalent) under the laws of its jurisdiction of incorporation or organisation. It has the full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each Transaction, and has taken all necessary corporate, regulatory, or other action to authorise such execution, delivery, and performance.

108: (b) No Violation. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and each Transaction do not and will not (i) violate or conflict with any provision of its constitutional or organisational documents (including, without limitation, its memorandum and articles of association, certificate of formation, limited liability company agreement, partnership agreement, or equivalent documents), (ii) violate or conflict with any applicable law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree of any governmental authority or regulatory body having jurisdiction over it, or (iii) result in a breach of, or constitute a default under, any agreement, instrument, or obligation to which it is a party or by which it or any of its assets may be bound.

This Agreement and each Transaction constitute legal, valid, and binding obligations of such party, enforceable against it in accordance with their respective terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganisation, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and to equitable principles of general applicability.

114: 9.2 Additional Seller Representation. Meridian Capital Securities LLC represents and warrants, as of the date of this Agreement and as of each Purchase Date, that it is duly registered as a broker-dealer with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under Section 15 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and is a member in good standing of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), CRD# 298417. 117: Paragraph 10(a) — Standard Events of Default
118: 10.1 Each of the following shall constitute an "Event of Default" with respect to a party (the "Defaulting Party"):

253: Section 7 — Margin Call Cut-off Time and Settlement
254: (a) The margin call cut-off time shall be 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day.

255: (b) If a Margin Call is given and received before 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day, the resulting transfer of Additional Purchased Securities, Equivalent Securities, or Cash Margin (as applicable) shall be effected on that same Business Day.

256: (c) If a Margin Call is given or received at or after 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the resulting transfer shall be effected on the next following Business Day.

257: (d) For the purposes of this Section 7, a Margin Call shall be deemed to have been "received" at the time of actual receipt by the addressee at the notice details specified in Section 14 of this Annex II. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to and acknowledge receipt of a Margin Call promptly upon receipt.
258: Section 8 — Netting

259: Paragraph 7(b) of the Agreement (settlement netting for obligations in the same currency falling due on the same settlement date) is elected and applicable. Accordingly, where on any Business Day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and on the same settlement date by each party to the other under this Agreement, such amounts shall be netted in accordance with Paragraph 7(b) of the Agreement, and only the resulting net amount shall be payable by the party owing such amount.
260: Section 9 — Substitution

261: (a) Seller may, from time to time during the term of any Transaction,   substitution of Alternative Securities for all or any part of the Purchased Securities in that Transaction. Any such   shall be made in writing (including by electronic mail) and shall specify in reasonable detail the Purchased Securities to be replaced, the proposed Alternative Securities (including ISIN, nominal amount, issuer, coupon, maturity, and credit rating), and the proposed substitution date.

264: (c) Where   substitution   effected  , by simultaneous transfer of the Alternative Securities to Buyer (or to Buyer's account at the relevant settlement system) and the Purchased Securities to Seller (or to Seller's account at the relevant settlement system), through the applicable settlement system in accordance with Paragraph 6.
265: (d) Alternative Securities must qualify as Eligible Collateral and must satisfy all of the eligibility criteria set out in Section 3 of this Annex II.

266: (e) Upon completion of a substitution, the Alternative Securities shall become the Purchased Securities for all purposes of the relevant Transaction, and the Confirmation for such Transaction shall be deemed to have been amended accordingly. For the avoidance of doubt, the occurrence of a substitution shall not affect the Purchase Date, the Repurchase Date, or the Pricing Rate of the relevant Transaction, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
267: Section 10 — Cross-Default
268: (a) For the purposes of Paragraph 10(a)(vi) of the Agreement, a "Cross-Default" shall occur with respect to a party if:

269: (i) such party fails to make any payment or delivery when due (after giving effect to any applicable grace period) under one or more agreements or instruments relating to Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold; or

270: (ii) such party's Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold is accelerated, or becomes capable of being accelerated, prior to its stated maturity as a result of a default (howsoever described) thereunder; or

271: (iii) any security interest securing Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold becomes enforceable and is enforced (including by the taking of possession or the appointment of a receiver, administrative receiver, manager, or other similar officer).

272: (b) "Specified Indebtedness" means any obligation (whether present or future, contingent or otherwise, as principal or surety or otherwise) in respect of borrowed money. For the avoidance of doubt, Specified Indebtedness includes obligations under loan agreements, credit facilities, overdraft facilities, note purchase agreements, bond indentures, guarantees of borrowed money, and similar instruments, but excludes obligations under this Agreement and under any other agreement that is a GMRA, GMSLA, or ISDA Master Agreement between the parties.
273: (c) "Cross-Default Threshold" means, with respect to each party,   (or its equivalent in any other currency, converted into the Base Currency at the spot rate of exchange at the relevant time).

274: (d) For the purposes of determining whether the Cross-Default Threshold has been exceeded, all amounts of Specified Indebtedness in respect of which the relevant event has occurred shall be aggregated (regardless of whether such amounts arise under the same or different agreements or instruments).
275: Section 11 — Act of Insolvency
276: (a) The definition of "Act of Insolvency" shall be as set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA, supplemented as follows.

278: (c) For the avoidance of doubt, and without limiting the definition of Act of Insolvency set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA, each of the following shall constitute an Act of Insolvency for the purposes of this Agreement:

279: (i) the appointment of a receiver, administrator, liquidator, conservator, trustee, custodian, or similar official over a party or any material part of its assets, whether by a court of competent jurisdiction, a governmental or regulatory authority, or otherwise;

281: (iii) the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors;
282: (iv) the admission in writing by a party of its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due;
283: (v) the taking of any corporate or other action by a party in furtherance of any of the foregoing; or
